newsitem.title: USA: Democrat hits Chicago Fed over unauthorized access.
newsitem.headline: Democrat hits Chicago Fed over unauthorized access.

text.p: A prominent Democratic lawmaker on Wednesday criticized the Chicago Federal Reserve Bank for allowing an outside economist to attend closed-door meetings where monetary policy was discussed.

In a letter to central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan, Rep. Henry Gonzalez asked why the university economist had been allowed to attend the meetings and queried whether such a practice was followed by other regional Fed banks.
"Only authorized Federal Reserve employees should have access to such information," said Gonzalez, a long-time Fed critic and ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee.
"Huge profits can be made with this information," the lawmaker added.

According to Gonzalez, Chicago Fed President Michael Moskow said he was informed by his General Counsel that allowing a consultant to attend the meetings was against Fed rule only after being asked about it by the Texas lawmaker.
The outside economist attended a discount rate briefing on January 9 and a monetary policy briefing on Feb. 3, according to information supplied to Gonzalez by Moskow.
Moskow was quoted by Gonzalez as saying that no classified Federal Open Market Committee materials were discussed at the Jan. 9 meeting.
At the Feb. 3 meeting, the FOMC's "Green Book" staff economic forecast was discussed but was not made available to the outside economist, Moskow told Gonzalez.
The Democratic lawmaker nevertheless said that the economist, who he did not name, could have gained inside information from his attendance at the meetings.
